# Oncology in Pets

Pets today face a serious threat from cancer that impacts millions of dogs and cats globally every year. Our oncology vet team provides advanced veterinary oncology care focused on early pet cancer diagnosis in the UAE and effective treatment plans tailored for each pet. A pet cancer diagnosis can be very stressful for many pet owners; however, our vet cancer specialist team focuses on fast diagnosis, clear guidance, and immediate treatment action.

Our veterinary team at Modern Vet offers comprehensive, compassionate and supportive oncology services to support you and your pet during the pet’s cancer diagnosis and treatment process.

## What Is Veterinary Oncology?

Veterinary oncology at our clinic focuses on how we diagnose, treat, and manage cancer to improve outcomes and quality of life. Veterinary oncology is a branch of veterinary medicine that concentrates solely on diagnosing and treating cancers in animals. The common treatments we provide are surgical interventions, chemotherapy, targeted therapies and palliative care. Our veterinary oncology team has experience working as vet oncology consultants and there is also a specialist dog cancer doctor in Dubai that pet owners can depend on for the best treatment options.

Our main goal is to maximize your pet’s quality of life for as long as possible. As such, our focus is on improving or maintaining your pet’s comfort level, ability to be active and enjoyment of daily activities during the course of their treatment.

Most Common Cancers
Found in Pets

At Modern Vet, we have veterinarians who are able to provide a diagnosis and treatment for a wide variety of different cancers found in pets. Our dog oncology specialist in Dubai and the cat oncology team focus on early detection and immediate treatment planning to improve survival rates. Early detection and treatment can greatly improve both the outcome and overall quality of life for your pet.

Lymphoma

The most common cancer of the lymphatic system in dogs and cats that causes swollen lymph nodes, lethargy, and loss of appetite. This detailed assessment helps identify areas requiring further investigation and provides valuable information for planning the most appropriate diagnostic tests and treatment.

Diagnostic Imaging

The Modern Vet utilizes state-of-the-art diagnostic imaging techniques to create images of tumors inside the body to determine the tumor’s size and location, as well as the extent of its spread. Our imaging services include digital X-rays, high-resolution ultrasound, CT scans and MRI technology. These detailed images allow our veterinary specialists to make faster, more accurate diagnoses and develop the most effective treatment plan for your pet.

Cytology and Biopsy

Cytology and biopsy are two diagnostic methods used to confirm cancerous conditions. During cytology, our veterinary staff will use a fine needle to collect cellular material from a mass or lesion for rapid evaluation. During a biopsy procedure, we will collect tissue samples from a mass, lymph node, or organ to examine under a microscope to make a final determination of the presence of cancer.

In-House Laboratory

Each of the MV Clinics is equipped with an in-hospital laboratory designed to perform a variety of diagnostic tests on an animal, including blood analysis, biochemical testing, cytology preparation, and many other important screening tests. If the veterinarian requires additional testing to be done outside of the clinic, the samples are sent to IDEXX reference laboratories located in the United Kingdom to analyze the samples further.

Blood and Urine Tests

It is very common for veterinarians to run a series of blood and urine tests before beginning a course of treatment such as chemotherapy or surgery to evaluate the animal’s overall health, detect any metabolic problems, and to see if there is any indication of organ damage. The results help ensure therapies are safe, effective, and tailored to your pet’s individual health status and medical needs.

Staging of Cancer

After cancer is confirmed by your veterinarian, it is necessary to stage the cancer to determine where the cancer is located in the body and how extensive the cancer is. Staging typically involves some combination of imaging studies, laboratory tests and/or tissue sampling. Proper staging of cancer enables vet oncology consultants to provide you with the most effective and individualized treatment plan for your pet.

## Comprehensive Oncology Treatment Options

MV Clinics provides specialized veterinary oncology services provided by Dr Beatriz that include but are not limited to chemotherapy, surgical oncology and palliative care to help improve the quality of life of your pet and their long term survival of cancer.

01

Treatment Planning

Each pet's cancer diagnosis is unique in that there are many different types of tumors. Treatment options for your pet will be based on the type of tumors your pet has, the stage of your pet's cancer, and your pet's overall health. Most importantly, all decisions are made to preserve and enhance your pet's quality of life as you move through each part of their care process.

02

Surgical Oncology

Surgery is the primary treatment for many solid tumors. Our team performs pet tumor removal Dubai using advanced surgical techniques to remove tumors while sparing as much surrounding healthy tissue as possible.

03

Chemotherapy

Chemotherapy is commonly used for systemic cancers (such as lymphoma) or in conjunction with surgery. Veterinary chemotherapy is designed to control cancer maintaining a good quality of life for your pet throughout treatment.

04

Targeted Therapy

Targeted therapies address only the targeted area in which the cancer resides. Thus, treatments will have a reduced effect on normal tissue. This method may result in better clinical responses for your pet as well as support their quality of life during treatment.

05

Palliative and Supportive Care

If there are no longer any viable options available for treating your pet's cancer, supportive care focuses on making your pet as comfortable as possible using pain relief, controlling nausea, promoting your pet's appetite, and providing hospice care.

## Frequently Asked Questions

How is cancer in pets diagnosed?

Veterinary cancer diagnosis is often accomplished with a physical examination, radiographs or ultrasound, lab tests, and cytological or biopsy testing. Our pet cancer diagnosis UAE approach focuses on fast, accurate and complete evaluation to begin treatment without delay.

## 

About The
Veterinary Referral Centre

The Veterinary Referral Centre (TVRC) is more than a hospital; it’s a movement that aims to transform the field of veterinary medicine in the UAE. Founded by Mansoor Alshiha, CEO of Vet Alliance, TVRC is the country’s first facility designed specifically for referral-only, specialty veterinary medicine. This facility is intended to fill a void within the veterinary care provided across the UAE, bridging the gap between local service and global standard of excellence, delivering specialized clinical expertise, state-of-the-art diagnostics, and professional training.

## Referral-Only Care and Specialisms

## Referral-Only Care and Specialisms

TVRC adopts a referral-only approach that empowers board-certified experts (diplomates of surgery, neurology, oncology, imaging, and others) to devote their efforts solely to managing complex and difficult cases. With state-of-the-art facilities, i.e., mCT scans, MRIs, and fully equipped surgical suites, the hospital is designed to provide the highest quality diagnostics and treatment.
TVRC does not provide routine services such as first opinions or vaccinations. Each patient presents at TVRC after being referred from another clinic. Therefore, there is always a specialist available for urgent and exceptional cases. This has produced a market shift and established a new standard in which general practitioners depend on experts for anything outside their routine practice.

## What Makes Us Unique

TVRC differentiates itself in a few key areas:

### Referral-Only Expertise

We offer highly specialized veterinary care for pets requiring advanced diagnostics, surgery, oncology, internal medicine, neurology, cardiology, and more. This model of referral-based care allows our team to do what we excel at to solve the most complex cases.

### Multidisciplinary Team

Our veterinary team consists of board-certified specialists with highly trained veterinary professionals from different disciplines. Each member has international training and experience to ensure the world-class practice and management of challenging medical and surgical conditions.

### Advanced Facilities

TVRC has state-of-the-art diagnostic equipment, surgical suites, and ICU-level monitoring for critical care patients. Our hospital has advanced imaging (MRI, CT, digital X-ray), well-equipped laboratories, and everything needed to provide fast, thorough diagnosis and treatment interventions.

## Our Services

Every patient referred to TVRC receives an individualized care plan developed by the appropriate specialist or multidisciplinary clinical team. Our services include:

  * Soft Tissue Surgery & Orthopedics

  * Neurology & Neurosurgery

  * Diagnostic Imaging – CT, MRI & Ultrasound

  * Oncology & Chemotherapy

  * Cardiology

  * Internal Medicine

  * Endoscopy & Minimally Invasive Procedures

  * Rehabilitation & Physiotherapy

Each case starts with thorough diagnostics and an expert consultation by one of our specialists, as well as a shared treatment planning process with your veterinarian.

Cancer is one of the most significant health challenges facing pets today, affecting millions of dogs and cats worldwide each year. A cancer diagnosis for your beloved companion can be pretty daunting and emotional, but at Modern Veterinary Hospital, we are here to help you through the process. Our veterinary oncology team can provide hope and care for your pet. As one of the most advanced cancer care centres in the UAE, your pet will have the best chance at a longer and happier life.

## Here Are Key Warning Signs That May Indicate Cancer In Your Pet:

Unexplained Lumps Or Bumps

### Soft Tissue Sarcomas

These tumors are not cancerous and come from connective tissues. They can be seen as firm yet painless lumps under the skin. In all cases, the main form of treatment involves surgical excision.

### Hemangiosarcoma

This tumor is a cancer of blood vessel cells that frequently develops in the spleen or heart, causing the animal to collapse suddenly from internal bleeding. While both surgery and chemotherapy can prolong life expectancy, the prognosis is generally poor.

### Mammary (Breast) Cancer

Mammary Tumors – Prevalent in unspayed female dogs and cats, generally benign or malignant. Since early surgical removal provides the best prognosis for cure, and spaying before the first heat cycle significantly reduces risk.

### Oral Tumors

Tumors such as squamous cell carcinoma and malignant melanoma that are found in the mouth can lead to halitosis, bleeding, and trouble eating. The treatment includes surgery and occasionally chemotherapy.

## Comprehensive Treatment Options

Each pet and each type of cancer is different. Our oncology team individualises treatment plans by assessing your pet’s type and stage of cancer, age, general health, and your family’s goals.

### Surgery

The first line of therapy for solid tumors is usually surgical resection. Our experienced surgeons can perform tumor dissections using the latest technology while minimizing damage to healthy tissue. Sometimes, surgery can be definitive; other times, it’s combined with other therapies.

### Chemotherapy

Chemotherapy directly works against systemic cancers such as lymphoma and is an adjunct to surgery. Chemotherapy for dogs is generally well-tolerated and has fewer side effects compared to human medicine. We closely monitor your pet for adverse reactions and adjust protocols as necessary.

### Targeted Therapies and Immunotherapy

Newer therapies include targeted therapies and immunotherapies, drugs, or antibodies that specifically attack cancer cells while doing minimal damage to normal cells. Modern Veterinary Hospital offers some of these therapies.

### Palliative and Supportive Care

If not, we focus on optimising comfort and quality of life. These can be pain control, nausea medications, appetite stimulants, hospice care, etc.
